text:
maya: dropping a new compact draft for the autoscale panel. focus: presets (latency/cost), burst behavior explanation, and how we surface guardrails. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/NEWPRESET/autoscale-presets liam: nice. first thought: presets are great for onboarding but we need to make it obvious they prefill values not lock them. sara: microcopy: label presets as 'Recommended profiles' and add small link 'What this changes' that expands a 1-line summary per preset. ethan: accessibility: presets should be keyboard operable and announce when applied via aria-live. also ensure the burst toggle has an accessible name and state. olivia: product question: do presets adjust both min/max and SLO slider, or just SLO? I think they should propose all relevant knobs with a 'Apply recommendation' affordance. maya: proposal: presets prefill min/max, SLO target, and suggest quantization. they show a small "confidence" tag (high/medium/low) based on telemetry. ben: burst UX: we need a clear explainer inline: short sentence + learn more. when burst is disabled (e.g., min==max or pool incompatible) show a tooltip explaining reason. arun: implementation note: when a preset is clicked, show a diff preview in the summary row (cost delta / SLO delta / peak with burst). keep it reversible. liam: visuals: prefer the preset chips stacked horizontally with short labels (e.g., Low-latency, Balanced, Cost-optimized) and a small info icon that opens detail. sara: copy tweak: change 'burst' label to 'short-term spikes (burst)' on first mention so new users understand tradeoff. ethan: aria snippet for announcement:
Applied preset: Balanced. Estimated monthly cost: $12.40 (approx.)
olivia: guardrails: three tiers. info (ok), warning (SLO increases > X%), block (violates guardrail). warnings should offer a one-click "auto-fix" suggestion. maya: agree. also include an "expert mode" toggle to expose cooldowns and prewarm counts for advanced teams. ben: pool selection: show pool capability badges (burst-supported, prewarm-available) and disable presets that require features the selected pool doesn't have. arun: backend: capture the preset id and assumptions snapshot in the rollout event for auditing and rollback. liam: UX nit: if preset changes both SLO and quantization, add a tiny pill showing "Q: 4-bit" so users see quantization impact on cost. sara: accessibility nits: preset chips need focus rings, 44px hit targets, and text contrast checks. info icon must have aria-label. maya: question: should we animate the diff preview numbers when a preset is selected? subtle count-up helps comprehension. ethan: yes, animate with easing and small duration. ensure motion respects reduced-motion preference. olivia: copy for disabled-burst tooltip: 'Burst unavailable: increase max or select a pool that supports burst.' actionable and short. ben: mobile: preset chips should wrap and the diff preview becomes a vertical section below them. arun: QA scenarios: apply preset then edit min/max, switch pools mid-edit, enable expert knobs, and apply during high traffic. sara: microcopy for presets detail: add a short "tradeoffs" line, e.g., 'Low-latency: lower 99p latency, higher cost.' keep it one sentence. maya: action items: - sara: finalize microcopy for presets and tooltips - ben + arun: pool badge spec + backend event capture - ethan: aria-live announcements + reduced-motion - liam: animations + visual polish - olivia: guardrail thresholds + auto-fix suggestions deploy-bot: uploaded image -> presets-panel-v1.png maya: thanks all 44d. I'll update figma and open a PR with the acceptance criteria. aiming for UX sign-off next Tue. ping in thread with any follow-ups.
